model_purpose: falsify the structural logic of shared modular infrastructure; not forecast deployment

edge_compute_slot.reason: general compute can be time-sliced only when latency, tenant isolation and local fallback gates pass

qualified_supervision:technical.reason: qualified staff can cover non-simultaneous technical tasks within an explicit span of control

qualified_supervision:accessibility.reason: competence and duty of care cannot be substituted by generic technical supervision

qualified_supervision:event.reason: event command remains a separate operational responsibility

sensor_module:camera_aggregate.reason: module is exchangeable only with privacy reset and calibration

sensor_module:environment_kit.reason: general environmental module can serve repeated tasks after calibration

sensor_module:lidar_local.reason: standardized mount permits exchange after safety calibration

sensor_module:uwb_localization.reason: receivers and bounded anchor coverage can support multiple tasks only within a calibrated cell

energy_port:low_voltage.reason: common protected interface; battery packs and high-energy systems remain platform-certified

maintenance_bay:general.reason: general inspection and safe recovery bay can serve compatible clean platforms sequentially

storage:general.reason: general dry storage can be scheduled and cleared between compatible tasks

storage:clean_payload.reason: payload storage needs cleanable separated lockers

storage:human_contact.reason: human-contact equipment needs segregated certified storage

storage:hazardous.reason: hazardous tools/materials require dedicated controlled storage

cleaning:general.reason: general wash-down is time-shareable after documented reset

cleaning:hygiene.reason: human-contact hygiene chain cannot share a generic wash zone

cleaning:contaminated.reason: contamination control requires a dedicated process and waste route

safe_isolation:general.reason: a lockable recovery position can be reused only after reset and incident closure

safe_isolation:human_contact.reason: duty-of-care and hygiene boundary requires segregated recovery

safe_isolation:hazardous.reason: hazard isolation and waste handling require dedicated containment

public_accountability_interface.reason: one staffed/status interface can explain sequential low-risk tasks but cannot replace task-specific duty holders

tool:assistive_contact_tool.reason: human-contact, hygiene and certification boundary requires segregation

tool:maintenance_tool.reason: hazard and contamination boundary requires task-specific control

tool:environment_probe.reason: calibrated probe can support repeated public observations

tool:event_av_module.reason: temporary module can be pooled outside event peaks

staggered_ordinary_day.interpretation: Distributed pooling beats duplication under this demand timing and the stated synthetic penalties.

coincident_event_peak.interpretation: Coincidence, modular overhead and shared failure exposure erase the distributed-pooling benefit under this profile.

universal_station_test.reason: A single pooled domain can be economically compact under some synthetic profiles but fails the correlated-failure admission gate.
universal_station_test.retained_pattern: distributed service cells + selected specialised backends + lightweight public accountability interfaces

failure_isolation.dedicated: one station failure is bounded to one task family in this abstraction
failure_isolation.shared: one cell failure affects tasks routed through roughly 1/2 of the pooled system
failure_isolation.design_requirement: shared infrastructure must be split into isolatable cells with manual recovery; a single central mega-hub is rejected

edge_compute_slot_unavailable.required_spatial_response: local stop controls, paper/manual task records and an operator room; no public route depends on the edge rack

one_shared_failure_cell_unavailable.required_spatial_response: physically independent shutdown zones, a manual recovery route and no single fire/power domain across all cells

power_constrained.required_spatial_response: protected life-safety loads, safe parking/isolation, non-powered public service and staged restart; no charging queue in public space

network_unavailable.required_spatial_response: local bounded operation only where pre-authorised, offline status display, staffed help and ordinary non-digital routes

shared_resource_contamination.required_spatial_response: separate clean/human-contact/hazardous stores, wash and waste routes; affected cell closes without contaminating the public frontage

operator_capacity_exceeded.required_spatial_response: visible queue cap, pause rule, staff welfare/oversight room and no automation that outruns qualified human supervision

conclusions: The shared object is a bounded set of compatible compute, energy, generic/special sensing, tooling, general maintenance, storage, cleaning, isolation and accountability resources—not every resource.
Assistive contact tools, hazardous tooling, hygiene/contamination stores and safety-specific supervision remain segregated even when co-located.
Distributed shared modular capacity can reduce duplication when peaks are staggered, but can be worse during coincident peaks after modular, routing and failure penalties.
Task requirements can eliminate sensors that exceed accuracy/TTL needs or the privacy ceiling; more sensing is not automatically preferred.
A universal station creates unacceptable correlated loss even when its synthetic cost index is attractive; spatial distribution and safe manual recovery are core urban requirements.
